lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: borrowing and returning responsibly

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 5: Planning, Belongings, and Communication
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice borrowing and returning responsibly. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: The learner identifies something real they want or need to borrow from someone else in the household, such as a tool, a book, or a piece of equipment.
safetyNotes: Before borrowing, the learner asks the item's owner directly and states the specific return time out loud, rather than assuming it is fine to take.
The item is checked for its condition (clean, undamaged, all pieces present) both right before borrowing and right before returning, so any change is caught honestly.
If the agreed return time cannot be met, the correct move is to tell the item's owner before the deadline passes, not after.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real item is available to borrow, the learner instead writes a detailed borrowing plan for a specific item they could realistically borrow in the future: who they would ask, the exact condition they would note beforehand, the return time they would propose, and one specific thing they would do differently from a time they forgot to return something or returned it in worse condition.

materials: adult-or-local: a real item belonging to someone else in the household
learner-local: paper or a notes app to record the agreement and the condition check

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain why agreeing on a specific return time and checking condition before you borrow, rather than after, makes it easier to return something responsibly.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Borrowing agreement: Permission is asked directly, a specific return time is agreed on, and the item's condition is noted before borrowing. | Return follow-through: The item is returned on time, or a late return is communicated to the owner before the deadline passes, and condition is honestly compared to the before-notes. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner track a second borrowing agreement where they are the lender instead of the borrower, noting the same before-and-after condition and timing details, and compare in writing what felt different about being on the lending side.

resources.title: borrowing and returning responsibly worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner identifies something real they want or need to borrow from someone else in the household, such as a tool, a book, or a piece of equipment.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact borrowing and returning responsibly decision or action.
Model move 2: Before asking to borrow anything, think about the item you have in mind.
Model move 3: Ask the owner directly for permission, agree on a specific return time, and note the item's condition before you take it.

Model check: Borrowing agreement: Permission is asked directly, a specific return time is agreed on, and the item's condition is noted before borrowing. | Return follow-through: The item is returned on time, or a late return is communicated to the owner before the deadline passes, and condition is honestly compared to the before-notes.

resources.title: borrowing and returning responsibly coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner identifies something real they want or need to borrow from someone else in the household, such as a tool, a book, or a piece of equipment.
Coach direction: Before asking to borrow anything, think about the item you have in mind.
Learner prompt: Name the item, who it belongs to, and why you want to borrow it.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: borrowing and returning responsibly complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Ask the owner directly for permission, agree on a specific return time, and note the item's condition before you take it.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I asked permission out loud instead of just taking the item.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I agreed on a specific return time (a day and roughly what time), not a vague 'later.'
Response 3 (t2-p3): I wrote down the item's condition before borrowing it.

Equal-access rule: If no real item is available to borrow, the learner instead writes a detailed borrowing plan for a specific item they could realistically borrow in the future: who they would ask, the exact condition they would note beforehand, the return time they would propose, and one specific thing they would do differently from a time they forgot to return something or returned it in worse condition.

resources.title: borrowing and returning responsibly minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain why agreeing on a specific return time and checking condition before you borrow, rather than after, makes it easier to return something responsibly.

Success checks: Borrowing agreement: Permission is asked directly, a specific return time is agreed on, and the item's condition is noted before borrowing. | Return follow-through: The item is returned on time, or a late return is communicated to the owner before the deadline passes, and condition is honestly compared to the before-notes.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: borrowing and returning responsibly supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional borrowing and returning responsibly condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Borrowing agreement: Permission is asked directly, a specific return time is agreed on, and the item's condition is noted before borrowing. | Return follow-through: The item is returned on time, or a late return is communicated to the owner before the deadline passes, and condition is honestly compared to the before-notes..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
